title: What Is Methylation and How Does It Affect Your Health? - ScienceInsights
abstract:
One of the most striking discoveries in recent years is that methylation patterns change predictably as you age. Researchers have built “epigenetic clocks” based on DNA methylation at specific sites across the genome. A comparison between newborns and centenarians found that roughly 87% of the regions that changed with age were losing methylation, not gaining it.

Studies in pregnant women have shown that supplementing with methylfolate raises blood folate levels more quickly and consistently than the same dose of folic acid, without producing unmetabolized folic acid in the blood.
The active form, called 5-MTHF or methylfolate, bypasses this entire conversion process. It’s absorbed and used directly, regardless of MTHFR status.
For people with MTHFR variants, methylfolate is the more reliable option since their reduced enzyme function makes converting folic acid even harder.
